caption: The video captures a vertical stack of white-painted metal channel profiles resting on a round yellow-and-black press base, with a dark circular platen bearing down on the column set against a pale workshop wall. The upper section already shows accordion-like buckled folds, so the crushing is ongoing rather than beginning. Over time, the platen bears down and the lower channels deform progressively. The pre-folded channels above keep their accordion creases while the deformation concentrates lower. The C-channel third from the bottom holds a diagonal inward fold of its top flange that deepens steadily. The channel second from the bottom shows its right-side wall bulging outward into a rounded white dome that grows pronounced over time. The bottom-most channel's top edge becomes visibly distorted. Throughout, the stack stays horizontally centered while the wall highlight and right-side shadow remain fixed, so the visible changes are object deformation rather than camera motion.
relations: Platen bearing down on the stack causes progressive deformation of lower channels while upper accordion folds persist.
Third-from-bottom C-channel develops a deepening diagonal inward fold of its top flange.
Second-from-bottom channel's right-side wall bulges outward into a growing rounded white dome.
Bottom channel's top edge distorts as the stack remains centered against fixed wall highlight and shadow.
